implementation_notes: Swift page objects wrap XCUITest: the test launches an XCUIApplication proxy (itself an XCUIElement subclass) and a page struct or class exposes computed properties and methods built from element queries (app.textFields["login_user"], app.buttons["Sign In"]), while XCTest's assertions stay in the test. What replaces the classic structure is the framework's element hierarchy plus Swift's computed properties; there is no POM library, so keeping queries in one place per screen is a discipline, and typed navigation is modelled by returning the next page type. Prefer accessibility identifiers over visible labels so queries survive copy changes.
pitfalls: XCUIElement queries are lazy and re-evaluate, but a reference kept across navigation resolves against the current hierarchy and can match a different element; express queries as computed properties.
XCUITest interactions block on the app's UI thread with its own timeouts, so failures must be driven by XCTest expectations (waitForExistence) rather than immediate assertions on element state.
Accessibility identifiers are part of the app-under-test's contract; when they change, the page object has to change in the same commit as the app.
